opportunities.title: Can a small model recognise the conditions hidden inside an “approval”?
opportunities.intro: Study a task-specific model that flags conditional, ambiguous or superseded approval text for human review. It must never authorise a merge or infer who actually made a decision.
opportunities.why_now: The October 19 case study reports a concrete mismatch between review wording and recorded approval state.
flow: Rules vs small pretrained text model
opportunities.question: Does adapting a small text encoder improve conditional-approval recall over rules, while keeping false alarms low on unseen phrasing and projects?
opportunities.experiment: Compare regex/rules, TF-IDF + logistic regression, frozen sentence embeddings and a small adapted encoder. Split by author/template and scenario family; measure precision, recall, calibration and abstention coverage. Include negation, resolved conditions and harmless suggestions.
opportunities.data: First create a labelled synthetic feasibility set; it cannot establish real-world performance. A thesis requires consented or appropriately licensed review examples, independent annotation and a leakage-safe held-out set. These are not secured yet.
opportunities.first_week: Produce annotation guidelines, 50 independently checked pilot cases and a baseline confusion matrix. Stop if reviewers cannot agree on labels or rules already solve the task.
opportunities.venture: Possible reviewer-assistance component for an AI-Org reliability service. No buyer demand or standalone market is established.
opportunities.alternatives: GitHub already supports requested changes and independent review; the case study recommends those practices. This would be an aid for ambiguous legacy text, not a replacement for proper controls.
opportunities.difference: Our proposed contribution is a bounded comparison of extraction and abstention under wording shift. It is not invention of conditional review or secure approvals.
opportunities.kill: Drop if a closest-work search finds the same evaluation, real data cannot be obtained, or a simple rule performs equally well. LTU supervisor acceptance and study design remain to confirm.

opportunities.title: Does a contamination detector confuse familiarity with prior exposure?
opportunities.intro: Stress-test existing forecasting-model audit methods with controlled examples that separate exact prior exposure from unseen series sharing the same generating process.
opportunities.why_now: The October 15 model release and October 17 disclosure question make evaluation uncertainty current. September research and the older TSFMAudit method are essential counterevidence.
opportunities.question: Under a fixed local compute budget, how reliably do adaptation-based audits separate deliberately exposed sequences from new same-process sequences?
opportunities.experiment: Use small, dated synthetic series generated after model release and controlled adaptations with known exposure. Compare static loss, candidate-only probes and reference-debiased probes. Hold out generating-process families. Measure false-positive rate on unseen familiar processes, sensitivity and compute cost.
opportunities.data: Original synthetic generators allow known exposure in the controlled adaptation stage. They do not reveal a foundation model’s actual pretraining corpus. Verify one checkpoint licence and implementation access before downloads; no paid compute.
opportunities.first_week: Inspect the existing audit implementation, map exactly what it already tests, and time one smallest-model probe. Produce a go/no-go report. No full benchmark or large-model fine-tuning in week one.
opportunities.venture: Could inform a specialist model-evaluation service for customer-specific deployments. Commercial value is hypothetical; do not sell contamination certificates.
opportunities.alternatives: TSFMAudit already debiases for dataset difficulty and tests transformed duplicates. The September study already discusses domain familiarity. A generic contamination benchmark would duplicate prior work.
opportunities.difference: The proposed test targets known adaptation exposure versus new same-process samples under a small compute budget. Whether this adds anything beyond existing ablations must be established first.
opportunities.kill: Drop if existing code already covers the proposed distinction, controlled ground truth cannot isolate the factor, or even the smallest probe exceeds laptop resources.
opportunities.scope: Non-LLM model adaptation / evaluation. Higher feasibility risk than RT1; research-only until the pilot passes.

opportunities.title: A read-only review-evidence checkup for teams using coding agents
opportunities.intro: Turn a repository’s exported review events into a small, inspectable report of what is supported, contradicted or unknowable. Sell the usefulness of the review, not a claim that AI can prove human judgement.
opportunities.why_now: October case evidence makes this timely; existing GitHub guidance and Kosli mean the opportunity, if any, is a lightweight diagnostic service.
flow: Check revision, time and stated conditions
opportunities.question: Would a small team use this report to change one concrete review or credential practice?
opportunities.experiment: Implement fixtures for stale approvals, checks finishing after merge, ambiguous actor identity and conditional text. Compare findings against manual inspection and native GitHub controls. The report must say unknown when evidence is missing.
opportunities.data: Start with synthetic event bundles and this owner’s explicitly selected test repository if later authorised. No employer data, secret scanning, production permissions or automatic repository changes.
opportunities.first_week: Build a complete local import → evidence timeline → export journey in 3–5 days, with a documented fixture suite and a walkthrough. A later owner-led trial with two maintainers tests usefulness.
opportunities.venture: Potential fixed-scope setup/reliability review for small development teams; repeat maintenance only if customers identify recurring value. No willingness-to-pay evidence yet.
opportunities.alternatives: GitHub rulesets and identity separation prevent many failures. Kosli already collects delivery evidence. Prefer configuring existing tools when that solves the problem.
opportunities.difference: A narrow, local diagnostic and onboarding deliverable. It is explicitly an integration/service hypothesis, not a new approval protocol or compliance certification.
opportunities.kill: Drop if the report adds nothing beyond native settings or an existing tool’s report, or maintainers will not use it. Do not build another general agent platform.
opportunities.scope: One-week product experiment; deterministic checks first. Optional classifier only after RT1 evidence supports it.

findings: Collector fetches public metadata, not full papers or discussion resolutions. This is suitable for leads, not recommendations.
Old digest sorted by first_seen and sampled six rows/source. It did not enforce publication-age windows.
Atom updated and Hugging Face lastModified could masquerade as publication dates. Existing records refreshed only last_seen, freezing stale metadata.
Curated public cards are exported separately from private worker briefs. There is no automatic semantic reconciliation; T6 counterevidence stayed in the private brief.
Worker research is bounded to roughly 12 minutes. Its source/read-depth limitations must survive into the dashboard, not disappear behind review_ready.
Schema/unit tests verify software contracts, not truth, research novelty, trend or commercial value.

collection.note: Counts by source include duplicate provenance. Dates are feed assertions pending primary-source verification. Eight empty channels are coverage gaps, not successful research.

limits: This is an initial evidence audit, not a systematic literature review or LTU topic approval.
No new opportunity passed validation. No customer interviews, experiments, model downloads or dataset trials were performed.
Read scope is explicit per source. Abstract-only and inaccessible sources cannot establish novelty or unresolved status.
Trend is not established for any lead; longitudinal independent signals are missing.
Broad live metadata covers many domains, but this manual audit prioritised existing cards and a small cross-domain sample.
changes: Server-side hold blocks enqueue and new claims in both lanes; existing running work, selections and artifacts are preserved.
Scheduled agents are in audit mode; collections continue while recommendations/default builds remain held.
Digest now prioritises publication-age buckets: 30-day leads, 90-day corroboration, separate old/modified/unknown/future records.
Publication and verification dates must be shown separately. A current read does not make an old source new.
